_about: Plato in English: Benjamin Jowett's complete translation of the dialogues (3rd ed., Oxford, 1892), public domain. One translator's whole Plato. Gutenberg texts are clean and carry Jowett's introductions and analyses; the Internet Archive set is the 1892 Clarendon five-volume collected edition (Royal College of Physicians copy) as raw OCR, kept as the page-citable edition of record and for the general index in vol. 5. Order: Gutenberg > Internet Archive. English only; no Greek. Translator recorded per title. Alcibiades II and Eryxias in Jowett's edition were translated by his secretary Matthew Knight (Jowett says so in the introduction to his second appendix). Two Jowett texts were already in the collection via the Adler shelf (Republic, Apology); they are cross-referenced, not refetched. Second translator, added 2026-10-02: the complete Bohn Works of Plato (Cary, Davis, Burges; 6 vols., 1848-54) as raw IA OCR, with vols. 1-2 also clean from Gutenberg (PG 78618, 79398). It carries the dialogues Jowett left out (Hipparchus, Minos, Rivals, Theages, Clitophon, Epinomis, the Epistles, Definitions and the other doubtful works). Third translator, added 2026-10-02: Thomas Taylor's complete Works of Plato (London, 1804; nine dialogues by Floyer Sydenham), 5 vols., raw IA OCR.

_cross_ref.plato-dialogues: pipeline/adler_shelf.json slug plato-dialogues = PG 1656, Jowett's Apology. Its shelf title says 'Apology, Crito, Phaedo', but PG 1656 holds the Apology only; Crito (PG 1657) and Phaedo (PG 1658) are on this shelf. This shelf's Apology points there instead of fetching it again

_translator_unchecked.plato-eryxias: Gutenberg's header names Jowett, whose edition it is; the text credits the translation of the spurious dialogues to his secretary, Mr. Knight (as the row says), so no single surname is checked against the header
_translator_unchecked.plato-alcibiades-2: Jowett's edition names no translator for this spurious dialogue; 'Mr. Knight' appears only as his secretary in the preface
